stories.headline: Grok Build's share links exposed 35,000 apps, including SpaceXSI's own internal sales files
stories.summary: Security firm Claroc found Grok Build's share links, meant to be unguessable, could be enumerated, opening 35,000 apps to anyone. Exposed data included medical exam results, employee ID numbers and a 594-account sales territory map from 24 SpaceXSI apps. Before your team shares anything built by a coding agent, check who can open the link.
stories.take: Link-only sharing on agent-built apps now counts as public hosting, where teams once treated it as private.

stories.headline: Microsoft researchers backdoor an AI agent by editing fewer than ten neurons, no retraining needed
stories.summary: Microsoft's Lazarus technique reprograms dormant neurons so an agent passes standard evaluations, then runs attacker code when a trigger appears, such as the clock passing midnight into 2027. Frontier agents can catch the edits, but only by comparing against the original weights. If provenance is your only defence, who verifies it in your deployment?
stories.take: Model procurement checks now need weight-integrity proof, because behavioural evaluations alone no longer certify a model as safe.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind's AI agents proved Signal's actual encryption code secure in four weeks
stories.summary: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code agents wrote millions of lines of Lean proofs showing Signal's compiled cryptographic code meets its security specifications, flagging just 1% for human review. Reintroduced real bugs were caught by machine-checked proofs, and the verification artifacts are open-sourced. If proofs take weeks, not years, which of your critical systems still rests on testing alone?
stories.take: Security assurance for critical code now takes weeks of agent-assisted proof, where it once took expert teams years.

stories.headline: The Bank for International Settlements built an AI agent that replicates central-bank economic models
stories.summary: Early signal that agentic coding tools can run macroeconometrics. The BIS paper pairs plain-text workflow files and a verified library of model specifications with an off-the-shelf coding agent.
